name: Mabel Batten
bio: Singer, known as "Ladye", 1856-1916. The Harry Ransom Center's biographical sketch of Radclyffe Hall calls her Hall's first lover and a "singer and society beauty" who "introduced her into a circle of artistic and intellectual women, many of them lesbians" - which places her, in the surviving record, as the person who brought Hall into queer society. She was the cousin of Una Troubridge, who met Hall in 1915 and became Hall's partner after Batten's death in 1916. Batten does not appear in Wilde's Complete Letters; her link to this map is through Hall.
bio_note: Dates (1856-1916) and the characterisation from the Harry Ransom Center finding aid for the Hall and Troubridge papers (eadid 00163), fetched and read in full 2026-08-03. No biography of Batten was consulted so far.
